Countries decided to resume deliberations in January in a reflection of the shared commitment and urgency needed to help make the world safer from future pandemics. title: New tools saved a million lives from malaria last year but progress under threat as drug resistance rises
summary: This year’s report provides a critical and up-to-date snapshot of efforts to control and eliminate malaria across 80 countries. The report also presents the threat posed by antimalarial resistance and its impact.

title: CEO of genetics firm says parents have a right to choose unborn child's traits
summary: Kian Sadeghi, the 25-year-old founder and CEO at Nucleus Genomics, tells "CBS Mornings" that parents have every right to select the qualities and traits they desire in their child.

title: How to avoid holiday stress
summary: The holiday season can be a wonderful, but also stressful time – filled with unrealistic expectations. A recent poll found 41% of adults anticipate more holiday stress this year. Psychiatrist Dr. Sue Varma has tips to unwind during the holidays.

title: San Francisco sues ultra-processed food makers
summary: In San Francisco on Tuesday, city attorney David Chiu announced the first government lawsuit of its kind against 11 companies that manufacture ultra-processed foods. Elizabeth Cook reports.

title: WHO issues global guideline on the use of GLP-1 medicines in treating obesity
summary: To address the growing global health challenge of obesity, which affects more than 1 billion people, WHO has released its first guideline on the use of Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 (GLP-1) therapies for treating obesity as a chronic, relapsing disease.

title: New prevention tools and investment in services essential in the fight against AIDS
summary: On World AIDS Day, the World Health Organization (WHO) calls on governments and partners to rapidly expand access to new WHO-approved tools including lenacapavir (LEN) to drive down infections and counter disruption to essential health services caused by cuts to foreign aid. Despite dramatic funding setbacks, the global HIV response has gained a remarkable…

title: WHO issues first global guideline on infertility
summary: The World Health Organization (WHO) today called on countries to make fertility care safer, fairer and more affordable for all in its first-ever global guideline for the prevention, diagnosis and treatment of infertility.Infertility is estimated to affect 1 in 6 people of reproductive age at some point in their lives.

title: These 19 cooking pans could leach lead into your food, FDA warns
summary: Consumers with the imported pans should throw them away due to the severe health risks posed by lead, the agency warns.

title: Doctor who criticized vaccines named CDC principal deputy director
summary: Louisiana Surgeon General Ralph Abraham, a critic of government vaccine mandates, has been quietly appointed to one of the CDC's top positions.

title: How Medicare's lower prices for 15 medications could impact your costs
summary: The Trump administration tapped a Biden-era rule to negotiate lower prices on 15 widely used medications for seniors.

title: Measles deaths down 88% since 2000, but cases surge
summary: Global immunization efforts have led to an 88% drop in measles deaths between 2000 and 2024, according to a new report from the World Health Organization (WHO). Nearly 59 million lives have been saved by the measles vaccine since 2000.

title: ClassPass founder's company reimagines classical Indian dance and helps young moms find community
summary: Payal Kadakia was just 27 when she came up with the idea for the popular app ClassPass, but it wasn't her first time building something from the ground up. In 2008, she created a dance company that reimagines classical Indian dance for a modern American audience.

title: ByHeart says all its baby formula could be tainted with botulism
summary: ByHeart said it can't rule out that all of its baby formula across all product lots could be contaminated, citing recent test results.

title: Doctor discusses cancer diagnosis for JFK's granddaughter, Tatiana Schlossberg
summary: This weekend, 35-year-old Tatiana Schlossberg, a granddaughter of former President John F. Kennedy, announced she has terminal cancer. CBS News medical contributor Dr. Celine Gounder has a breakdown of the diagnosis.

title: Powering our appetite for protein
summary: Proteins, whether from whey, plants or animals, are essential for building muscle. Last year, approximately 71% of consumers identified protein as the nutrient they most frequently try to eat. title: Lifetime toll: 840 million women faced partner or sexual violence
summary: Violence against women remains one of the world’s most persistent and under-addressed human rights crises, with very little progress in two decades, according to a landmark report released today by the World Health Organization (WHO) and UN partners. title: More countries report rising levels of drug-resistant gonorrhoea, warns WHO
summary: The World Health Organization (WHO) warns that gonorrhoea, a sexually transmitted infection, is becoming increasingly resistant to antibiotics, according to new data from its Enhanced Gonococcal Antimicrobial Surveillance Programme (EGASP), which monitors the spread of drug-resistant gonorrhoea. title: World marks cervical cancer elimination day as countries accelerate action
summary: Today marks the first World Cervical Cancer Elimination Day – mandated by the World Health Assembly – a historic milestone in global efforts to end a preventable cancer.

title: Death in N.J. believed to be 1st linked to meat allergy spread by ticks
summary: A New Jersey man is the first person believed to have died from alpha-gal syndrome, a meat allergy triggered by a tick bite, researchers say.

title: WHO promotes lifesaving intervention for small and preterm babies on first official World Prematurity Day
summary: The World Health Organization (WHO) is marking its first official observance of World Prematurity Day with the launch of a new global clinical practice guide for Kangaroo Mother Care (KMC) – a simple, proven and life-saving intervention that significantly improves survival for preterm and low birth weight babies. title: Marjorie Taylor Greene says "I don't see political party lines" on health care
summary: House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries called GOP Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene an ally during the shutdown for joining Democrats in demanding that Congress address high health care costs.

title: WHO and Brazil urge swift action on Belém Health Action Plan at COP30
summary: The COP30 Special report on health and climate change: delivering the Belém Health Action Plan, notes that rising temperatures and collapsing health systems are claiming more lives, and calls for immediate and coordinated action to protect health in a rapidly warming world. It follows the launch of the Belém Health Action Plan, a flagship initiative of Braz…

title: WHO launches global guidelines on diabetes during pregnancy on World Diabetes Day
summary: The World Health Organization (WHO) today released its first global guidelines for the management of diabetes during pregnancy, a condition affecting about one in six pregnancies – or 21 million women annually. The new recommendations provide a critical roadmap to tackle this growing health challenge and prevent serious complications for both women and thei…

title: New prediction breakthrough delivers results shockingly close to reality
summary: Researchers have created a prediction method that comes startlingly close to real-world results. It works by aiming for strong alignment with actual values rather than simply reducing mistakes. Tests on medical and health data showed it often outperforms classic approaches. The discovery could reshape how scientists make reliable forecasts.

title: Global gains in tuberculosis response endangered by funding challenges
summary: Tuberculosis (TB) remains one of the world’s deadliest infectious killers, claiming over 1.2 million lives and affecting an estimated 10.7 million people last year, according to the WHO Global Tuberculosis Report 2025, released today.

title: Egypt becomes the seventh country in the Eastern Mediterranean Region to eliminate trachoma as a public health problem
summary: The World Health Organization (WHO) today announced that Egypt has successfully eliminated trachoma as a public health problem, marking a historic public health milestone for the country and WHO’s Eastern Mediterranean Region (WHO EMR). It is the seventh country in WHO EMR to achieve this milestone. The validation of Egypt’s achievement brings the total num…

title: New FDA-approved eye drop aims to help adults with age-related vision issues
summary: The once-daily, prescription eye drop is said to help combat presbyopia.

title: Air pollution in India's capital draws protests as schools are shuttered
summary: India's capital Delhi is blanketed in toxic smog every autumn, but the pollution is already so bad that it's drawn protests as authorities tell students to stay home.

title: Extended interview: FDA chief calls warnings on menopause treatments an "American tragedy"
summary: FDA Commissioner Dr. Marty Makary tells CBS News' Norah O'Donnell in an exclusive interview why the agency decided to drop decades-old "black box" warnings on many hormone therapy drugs used for menopause and perimenopause symptoms.

title: FDA chief says warning labels deterred menopause care: "It's an American tragedy"
summary: In an interview with CBS News, FDA Commissioner Dr. Marty Makary explains what went into the decision to drop the most serious warnings on hormone therapy for menopause.

title: Baby formula recalled as CDC investigates cases of infant botulism
summary: The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention is investigating more than a dozen cases of infant botulism tied to the formula brand ByHeart, prompting a voluntary recall of the product. Officials say there have been 13 cases across 10 states since August. No deaths have been reported.

title: FDA chief explains changes to "black box" warnings on some hormone therapies for menopause
summary: FDA commissioner Dr. Marty Makary joins "CBS Mornings" to discuss the agency's announcement Thursday that boxed warnings will be removed from many estrogen products used for hormone therapy, a treatment that helps alleviate the symptoms of menopause.

title: Book excerpt: "The Day After Yesterday: Resilience in the Face of Dementia"
summary: Photographer Joe Wallace has chronicled the stories of families who have lived with Alzheimer's.

title: Countries make progress on WHO Pandemic Agreement annex on pathogen access and benefit sharing system
summary: In an important step, Member States started discussing for the first time the proposed draft text of the annex to the WHO Pandemic Agreement that establishes the Pathogen Access and Benefit Sharing (PABS) system. The PABS system is a key part of the global agreement adopted earlier in 2025 to make the world safer from future pandemics.

title: Joint call to strengthen policy and investment for child and youth mental health and well-being
summary: Despite increasing recognition of mental health across UN policy frameworks, children and youth remain largely absent from global commitments, data systems, and financing priorities.

title: WHO at the 151st IPU Assembly: advancing health, rights and resilience through parliamentary action
summary: WHO joined parliamentary leaders at the 151st Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) Assembly, held on 19–23 October 2025 in Geneva, bringing together nearly 1150 delegates, including over 600 members of parliament from 132 countries.

title: WHO issues guidance to address drastic global health financing cuts
summary: The World Health Organization (WHO) today released new guidance for countries on ways to counter the immediate and long-term effects of sudden and severe cuts to external funding, which are disrupting the delivery of essential health services in many countries. title: Stanford’s tiny eye chip helps the blind see again
summary: A wireless eye implant developed at Stanford Medicine has restored reading ability to people with advanced macular degeneration. The PRIMA chip works with smart glasses to replace lost photoreceptors using infrared light. Most trial participants regained functional vision, reading books and recognizing signs.
